title: Japan: 20 Days of Adventure, Culture & Flavor: Tokyo → Hakone → Kanazawa → Takayama → Kyoto → Nara → Osaka → Hiroshima → Miyajima → Osaka
description: An epic 20-day journey through Japan's iconic cities and hidden gems. From Tokyo's neon-lit streets to Kyoto's serene temples, Osaka's legendary street food, and Hiroshima's powerful history — this itinerary covers it all with the perfect balance of adventure, culture, and food.

days.title: Arrival & Shinjuku Exploration
days.description: Touch down in Tokyo and dive straight into the neon-lit energy of Shinjuku.

activities.name: Arrive at Narita/Haneda → Shinjuku
activities.description: Take the Narita Express (NEX) or Limousine Bus to Shinjuku. Activate your JR Pass at the airport.
details: 💡 NEX takes ~80 min from Narita, covered by JR Pass
tips: Drop bags at your hotel and explore — don't waste your first afternoon sleeping off jet lag.

activities.name: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane)
activities.description: Wander this atmospheric alley of tiny yakitori joints. Pull up a stool, order some skewers and a beer. Free observation decks on the 45th floor. Open until 11pm — stunning night views of the city.
details: 📍 West exit of Shinjuku Station

activities.name: Golden Gai Bar Crawl
activities.description: Pick 2-3 tiny bars to hop between. Each has a unique theme — from jazz to horror to anime. Look for bars without cover charges (check the signs).
details: 💡 Some bars charge ¥500-1000 cover. Ask before sitting.

days.title: Classic Tokyo: Markets, Temples & Neon
days.description: Hit Tokyo's iconic trio: the bustling Tsukiji market, ancient Senso-ji, and the electric streets of Akihabara.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
activities.description: Arrive early (8am) for the freshest sushi, tamagoyaki, and uni. Walk the narrow aisles sampling everything.
details: 📍 4-16-2 Tsukiji, Chuo City

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa
activities.description: Walk through Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), browse Nakamise-dori for traditional snacks and souvenirs, then explore the temple grounds. Multi-floor arcades, retro game shops, and anime stores. Visit Super Potato for vintage gaming or a maid café for the full experience.

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Shibuya Sky
activities.description: Experience the iconic crossing, then head up to Shibuya Sky for 360° rooftop views.
details: 💡 Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance — ¥2,000

days.title: Harajuku, Meiji Shrine & Roppongi Art
days.description: From Meiji Shrine's forest calm to Harajuku's kawaii chaos to Roppongi's art scene.

activities.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
activities.description: Walk through the towering torii gate into this peaceful forest shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Arrive early for a serene experience.
details: 📍 1-1 Yoyogikamizonocho, Shibuya

activities.name: Takeshita Street & Harajuku
activities.description: Kawaii culture epicenter — wild fashion, themed cafés, and the best crepes in Tokyo. Stroll this tree-lined boulevard and admire buildings by Tadao Ando, SANAA, and Toyo Ito.

activities.name: Mori Art Museum & Tokyo City View
activities.description: Contemporary art exhibitions plus a stunning open-air observation deck on the 52nd floor.
details: 💡 Open until 10pm — combine art and night views

days.title: Toyosu Market, teamLab & Tokyo Bay
days.description: Tuna auctions at dawn, barefoot digital art at teamLab, and a splurge sushi dinner in Ginza.

activities.name: Toyosu Fish Market
activities.description: Watch the famous tuna auction from the observation deck (arrive by 5:30am), then eat sushi breakfast at the market restaurants.
details: 💡 Book tuna auction viewing online — limited to 120 visitors/day

activities.name: teamLab Planets
activities.description: Walk barefoot through stunning immersive digital art installations. You'll wade through water, walk through flowers, and lose yourself in infinity rooms.
details: 💡 Book tickets online — sells out! Wear pants you can roll up.

activities.name: Ginza Evening Stroll
activities.description: Window-shop along Chuo-dori (closed to traffic on weekends). Visit the stunning Ginza Six department store.
tips: Splurge night! This is your fancy Tokyo dinner. Book well in advance.

days.title: Old Tokyo: Yanaka, Ueno & Sumo Culture
days.description: Explore old-school Tokyo in Yanaka, then catch the May Grand Sumo Tournament live!

activities.name: Ueno Park & Tokyo National Museum
activities.description: Japan's oldest and most comprehensive museum. The Japanese Gallery alone is worth 2 hours.
details: 💡 ¥1,000 entry — JR Pass doesn't cover this

activities.name: Yanaka District Walk
activities.description: Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhood. Wander past wooden houses, tiny temples, and cat statues. Yanaka Ginza street has great snacks. The May Basho runs May 10-24 at Ryogoku Kokugikan! Watch live sumo — one of Japan's most thrilling cultural experiences.
details: 💡 Book tickets at sumo.or.jp as soon as they open. Upper seats ~¥3,800, box seats ~¥11,000

days.title: Day Trip: Kamakura's Great Buddha & Coast
days.description: Escape to Kamakura's Great Buddha, coastal temples, and sunset on Enoshima Island.

activities.name: Train to Kamakura
activities.description: Take JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line from Shinjuku (~1hr, covered by JR Pass). Kamakura's grandest shrine, set at the end of a beautiful tree-lined approach.

activities.name: Great Buddha of Kamakura
activities.description: Stand before the serene 13-meter bronze Buddha, cast in 1252. You can go inside the hollow statue for ¥50. Beautiful temple with thousands of small Jizo statues and a stunning ocean view from the terrace.
details: 📍 Kotoku-in Temple · ¥300 entry

activities.name: Enoshima Island Sunset
activities.description: Take the Enoden tram to this small island. Climb to the top for panoramic Pacific views. Watch the sunset over Sagami Bay with Mt. Fuji in the background.
details: 💡 Enoden tram is not covered by JR Pass — ¥260 from Kamakura

days.title: Hakone: Hot Springs & Mt. Fuji Views
days.description: Hot springs, volcanic eggs, and Mt. Fuji views — Hakone is pure magic.

activities.name: Romance Car to Hakone
activities.description: Take the iconic Odakyu Romance Car from Shinjuku — reserved seats, big windows, Fuji views. Stunning outdoor sculpture garden with over 120 works set against mountain scenery. Don't miss the Picasso Pavilion.
details: 💡 ¥2,330 one-way, not covered by JR Pass but worth it
¥1,600 entry

activities.name: Hakone Loop: Ropeway → Owakudani → Lake Ashi
activities.description: Ride the ropeway over volcanic terrain to Owakudani. Eat the famous black eggs (said to add 7 years to your life!), then take the pirate ship across Lake Ashi.
details: 💡 Hakone Free Pass covers all transport in the loop — ¥6,100 from Shinjuku including Romance Car

activities.name: Ryokan & Onsen Experience
activities.description: Check into a traditional ryokan. Soak in the natural hot springs (onsen), wear a yukata, and enjoy a kaiseki dinner course.
details: 💡 Budget ~¥20,000-40,000/person including dinner and breakfast

days.neighborhoods: Kanazawa Station · Higashi Chaya · Omicho Market
days.title: Shinkansen to Kanazawa: Japan's Hidden Gem
days.description: Bullet train to Kanazawa — Japan's best-kept secret for sushi, gardens, and geisha culture.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Kanazawa
activities.description: Take the Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station (~2.5 hours). The route passes through mountains and tunnels.
details: 💡 Covered by JR Pass. Reserve seats in advance at a JR ticket office.

activities.name: Omicho Market
activities.description: Kanazawa's 'kitchen' since 1721. Try fresh crab, uni, and the famous kaisendon (seafood rice bowl). Wander the wooden-latticed teahouses of this Edo-era geisha district. Visit Kaikaro teahouse for gold-leaf tea.
details: 📍 Open 9am-5pm, some stalls close early

activities.name: Kenroku-en Garden Evening
activities.description: One of Japan's three most beautiful gardens. May brings irises and fresh green foliage. Wander the bridges, streams, and historic teahouses.
details: ¥320 entry · Open until 6pm in May

days.title: Kanazawa: Samurai, Gold Leaf & Craft
days.description: Samurai houses, gold leaf ice cream, and world-class contemporary art.

activities.name: Nagamachi Samurai District
activities.description: Walk the atmospheric earthen-walled lanes where samurai once lived. Visit the Nomura Samurai House for a peek inside.
details: Nomura House: ¥550 · Beautiful tiny garden rated in top Japanese gardens

activities.name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
activities.description: Leandro Erlich's Swimming Pool (you can look down into a room through 'water') is the star, but the whole museum is fantastic. Free areas + paid exhibitions. Kanazawa produces 99% of Japan's gold leaf. Visit Hakuza to see artisans hammer gold into impossibly thin sheets, then eat gold-leaf ice cream.
details: 💡 Free zones open until 10pm. Paid exhibitions ¥1,200.

activities.name: Kazuemachi Evening Walk
activities.description: The quieter geisha district comes alive at dusk. Stroll along the Asano River and listen for shamisen music drifting from teahouses.

days.neighborhoods: Takayama Old Town · Miyagawa Morning Market
days.title: Takayama: Edo Streets & Mountain Culture
days.description: Journey through the Japanese Alps to Takayama's perfectly preserved Edo streets.

activities.name: Train to Takayama
activities.description: Take the Wide View Hida limited express through the spectacular Japanese Alps. One of Japan's most scenic train rides. Stroll the riverside market for local pickles, miso, crafts, and fresh produce from the surrounding mountains.
details: 💡 ~2.5 hours from Kanazawa (transfer at Toyama). JR Pass covers it.
Open 6am-noon daily

activities.name: Sanmachi Suji (Old Town)
activities.description: Three streets of dark-wood merchant houses from the Edo period. Sake breweries marked by sugidama (cedar balls) above the door — duck in for tastings. Visit 2-3 of the six breweries on Sanmachi Suji. Look for the cedar ball signs. ¥200-500 gets you a tasting flight.

activities.name: Takayama Jinya
activities.description: The only surviving Edo-era government office. Beautiful tatami rooms and a torture chamber (yes, really).
details: ¥440 entry

days.title: Shirakawa-go & Journey to Kyoto
days.description: UNESCO village of Shirakawa-go, then an evening arrival in ancient Kyoto.

activities.name: Bus to Shirakawa-go
activities.description: Take the Nohi Bus from Takayama (50 min, ~¥2,600). Arrive at the UNESCO village of steep thatched-roof farmhouses nestled in the mountains. Walk among 114 traditional gassho-zukuri houses (named for the 'praying hands' roof shape). Visit Wada House museum and climb to Shiroyama Viewpoint.
details: 💡 Not covered by JR Pass. Book bus tickets in advance at Takayama Bus Center.

activities.name: Bus back to Takayama → Shinkansen to Kyoto
activities.description: Return to Takayama, then take the Wide View Hida to Nagoya and transfer to the Tokaido Shinkansen to Kyoto. Total ~4 hours.
details: 💡 All covered by JR Pass except Takayama-Shirakawa bus

activities.name: Arrive in Kyoto & Pontocho Alley
activities.description: Check into your hotel and stroll Pontocho — a narrow lantern-lit alley along the Kamo River packed with intimate restaurants.
tips: Kawadoko (riverside dining terraces) open in May. Request a terrace seat — it's magical at night.

days.title: Eastern Kyoto: Fushimi Inari & Kiyomizu
days.description: Fushimi Inari's 10,000 gates at dawn, Kiyomizu-dera, and geisha-spotting in Gion.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari at Dawn
activities.description: Arrive by 6am for the famous torii gate tunnels almost to yourself. Hike partway up the mountain (30-60 min) for incredible views.
details: 💡 Free entry, open 24/7. Early morning = no crowds.

activities.name: Nishiki Market
activities.description: Five blocks of Kyoto's culinary soul. Try yuba (tofu skin), tsukemono (pickles), matcha everything, and mochi. Perched on a hillside, this temple's massive wooden stage offers sweeping views of Kyoto. Walk the charming Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes to get there.
details: 📍 Nishiki-koji Dori · Most stalls close by 5pm
¥400 entry · Open 6am-6pm

activities.name: Gion District at Dusk
activities.description: Walk Hanamikoji-dori and the back streets of Gion. If you're lucky, you'll spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) hurrying to an evening engagement.
details: 💡 Be respectful — don't chase or block geiko/maiko for photos

days.title: Arashiyama: Bamboo, Monkeys & River
days.description: Bamboo groves, wild monkeys, and a hidden temple with 1,200 moss-covered statues.

activities.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
activities.description: Get here by 7am to experience the soaring bamboo without crowds. The morning light filtering through is magical. UNESCO site with one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens designed in the 14th century. The garden is the star — skip the interior.
details: 💡 Free · Take JR Sagano Line from Kyoto Station (15 min)
Garden ¥500 · Opens 8:30am

activities.name: Iwatayama Monkey Park
activities.description: Climb 20 min up the hill to hang out with 120 wild macaques. You feed them — they don't feed on you. Incredible city views from the top. 20-minute walk from the bamboo grove through quiet Sagano. 1,200 unique stone Buddhist statues covered in moss — each with a different expression. Few tourists make it here.
details: ¥550 entry
¥300 entry · One of Kyoto's best-kept secrets

activities.name: Sagano Scenic Railway
activities.description: Take the romantic open-air train along the Hozu River gorge. 25 minutes of beautiful scenery.
details: ¥880 · Runs from Saga-Torokko Station

days.title: Golden Temple, Zen Gardens & Cooking Class
days.description: Golden Pavilion, zen rock gardens, and a hands-on Japanese cooking class.

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
activities.description: Arrive at opening (9am) for the best photos. The gold-leaf covered pavilion reflecting in the pond is surreal. The enigmatic 15-stone rock garden — you can never see all 15 from any single vantage point. Sit and contemplate.
details: ¥500 entry · Your 'ticket' is a lucky charm
¥500 entry · 10-minute walk from Kinkaku-ji

activities.name: Japanese Cooking Class
activities.description: Hands-on class making dashi, sushi rolls, tempura, and miso soup. Learn techniques you'll use at home forever.
details: 💡 Book via Airbnb Experiences or WAK Japan · ~¥6,000-8,000/person

days.title: Day Trip: Nara's Deer & Ancient Temples
days.description: Day trip to Nara — friendly deer, the Great Buddha, and persimmon-leaf sushi.

activities.name: JR to Nara + Nara Park
activities.description: 45-min train from Kyoto (JR Pass). Deer greet you almost immediately. Buy shika senbei (¥200) and bow to the deer — they bow back!
details: 💡 Be careful — the deer can be aggressive for crackers. Raise your hands empty to show you're out.

activities.name: Todai-ji Temple
activities.description: Home to the Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — a 15-meter bronze statue inside the world's largest wooden building. The scale is breathtaking. Walk through the forest to this shrine famous for its 3,000 stone and bronze lanterns. In the inner sanctum, all lanterns are lit in the darkness.
details: ¥600 entry
¥500 for inner sanctum

activities.name: Naramachi Stroll
activities.description: Wander the old merchant quarter. Traditional machiya townhouses now house cafés, galleries, and craft shops.

days.title: Kyoto: Tea Ceremony, Philosophy Path & Farewell
days.description: Tea ceremony, Philosopher's Path, and a farewell evening on the Kamo River.

activities.name: Nanzen-ji Temple
activities.description: One of Kyoto's most impressive temples. Walk through the massive Sanmon gate and discover the surprising brick aqueduct — a relic of Japan's Meiji modernization. 2km stone path along a cherry-tree-lined canal connecting Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji. In May, lush green replaces the famous blossoms.
details: ¥600 for Sanmon gate · Grounds free
Free · Allow 45-60 min

activities.name: Tea Ceremony Experience
activities.description: Participate in a traditional matcha tea ceremony. A tea master guides you through every movement — it's meditative and deeply cultural. Buy exceptional matcha, sencha, and gyokuro to take home. Their tasting room lets you prepare and compare teas.
details: 💡 Camellia Tea Ceremony near Gion — ¥3,000/person, English-speaking host
📍 Teramachi-dori · Since 1717

activities.name: Kyoto Farewell at Kamo River
activities.description: Grab drinks and snacks and sit along the Kamo River banks. Locals gather here at sunset — it's Kyoto at its most relaxed.
tips: Last night in Kyoto. Take a moment at the Kamo River to reflect on the journey so far.

days.title: Osaka: Street Food Capital of Japan
days.description: Welcome to Osaka — Japan's street food capital. Kushikatsu, takoyaki, and Dotonbori at night.

activities.name: Train to Osaka + Osaka Castle
activities.description: Quick 15-min shinkansen from Kyoto (JR Pass). Drop bags, then visit the impressive castle and its expansive park.
details: ¥600 entry to main tower · Park is free

activities.name: Shinsekai District
activities.description: This retro neighborhood feels like 1960s Japan. Colorful signs, pachinko parlors, and the best kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) in the country.

activities.name: Dotonbori Street Food Marathon
activities.description: THE iconic Osaka experience. Neon signs reflecting in the canal, giant mechanical crabs, and endless food stalls. This is Japan's food capital.
details: 📍 Along Dotonbori Canal · Best after dark

days.title: Osaka: Kuromon Market, Umeda & Nightlife
days.description: Kuromon Market grazing, vintage shopping, and Osaka's legendary nightlife scene.

activities.name: Kuromon Market
activities.description: Osaka's 'Kitchen' — 170+ stalls selling everything from ¥1,000 tuna sashimi to ¥5,000 A5 wagyu on a stick, torched right in front of you.
details: 📍 Opens 9am · Best before noon

activities.name: Amerikamura & Vintage Shopping
activities.description: Osaka's Harajuku — thrift shops, street art, and the famous Triangle Park people-watching scene. Two towers connected by a rooftop 'Floating Garden' observatory. The escalator ride up through the void between towers is thrilling.
details: ¥1,500 entry · Open until 10:30pm

activities.name: Hozenji Yokocho
activities.description: Atmospheric narrow alley hidden behind Dotonbori. Splash water on the moss-covered Fudo Myo-o statue for good luck, then duck into a tiny bar.
tips: Osaka nightlife is legendary. Check out the bars around Ura-Namba for the local scene.

days.title: Day Trip: Hiroshima & Miyajima Island
days.description: A powerful day: Hiroshima's Peace Memorial and the floating torii gate of Miyajima Island.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Hiroshima
activities.description: 1.5 hours from Osaka via Nozomi (or Sakura/Hikari with JR Pass). Arrive by 9am. Walk through the park, see the Atomic Bomb Dome, visit the deeply moving museum. Allow 2 hours for the museum.
details: 💡 JR Pass covers Sakura/Hikari shinkansen. Nozomi requires a supplement.
¥200 museum entry · Profoundly impactful experience
tips: The Peace Museum is emotionally heavy. Take your time and be respectful. It's one of the most important places in the world.

activities.name: Ferry to Miyajima Island
activities.description: JR Ferry from Miyajimaguchi (15 min, covered by JR Pass). Spot the floating torii gate from the ferry! The iconic vermillion torii gate appears to float on water at high tide. Walk out to touch it at low tide. The shrine itself is built on stilts over the water.
details: 💡 Check tide times — torii gate is 'floating' at high tide, walkable at low tide. Both are special.
¥300 shrine entry

activities.name: Miyajima at Dusk
activities.description: After the day-trippers leave, Miyajima becomes magical. Deer roam the quiet streets, lanterns light up, and the torii gate glows.
details: 💡 If you have time, hike up Mt. Misen (1.5hrs) or take the ropeway for island panoramas

days.title: Final Day: Last Bites & Sayonara
days.description: Final takoyaki, last-minute shopping, and sayonara Japan.

activities.name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
activities.description: A unique shrine featuring a giant lion head stage (Ema-den). It's said to swallow evil spirits and bring good luck. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — Japanese snacks, matcha KitKats, and ceramics.
details: Free · 5 min walk from Namba Station

activities.name: Dotonbori — One Last Time
activities.description: Take your final photo with the Glico Running Man sign. Get one last round of takoyaki. Say goodbye to Osaka.
tips: Grab airport snacks at Don Quijote — tax-free shopping for tourists.

activities.name: Nankai Rapi:t to Kansai Airport
activities.description: Take the retro-futuristic Rapi:t express from Namba to KIX (50 min, ¥1,290). Or take the JR Haruka (covered by JR Pass) from Tennoji.
details: 💡 JR Haruka from Tennoji is covered by JR Pass if it's still active
tips: Sayonara, Japan! You've earned those 400,000 steps. Until next time. ✈️🇯🇵
